t:
The section analysis of chapter 135 of title 7, Canal Zone Code, preceding section 3081 of that title, is amended by striking out, in item numbered 8088, the word “investments”, and in lieu thereof inserting “investment”, so that the item will read:


“3088. Investment awl management of wards’ estates; orders of court.”.

fable.w: This section is a purely technical amendment correcting one word in a table-of-contents item of the Canal Zone Code. The mention of "orders of court" might look like judicial involvement, but it is only part of a section heading and grants no outside party a right to sue or be consulted. No party outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision.
fable.s: is amended by striking out, in item numbered 8088, the word “investments”, and in lieu thereof inserting “investment”

qwen_block.w: This section is a technical amendment to a table of contents or section analysis, correcting a typo from 'investments' to 'investment'. It does not establish any process for public participation, consultation, or coordination with outside parties. It is purely administrative and textual.
qwen_block.s: The section analysis of chapter 135 of title 7, Canal Zone Code, preceding section 3081 of that title, is amended by striking out, in item numbered 8088, the word “investments”, and in lieu thereof inserting “investment”, so that the item will read: “3088. Investment awl management of wards’ estates; orders of court.”.

opus.w: This is a clerical amendment that changes one word in a section heading of the Canal Zone Code. It creates no process for anyone outside the federal government to take part in a federal decision. The words "orders of court" are just part of the heading's title. They do not give any outside party a right to sue or to object to a decision.
opus.s: is amended by striking out, in item numbered 8088, the word “investments”, and in lieu thereof inserting “investment”
opus.b: The obvious wrong reading would be to treat "orders of court" and "wards' estates" as signs of a legal process that brings outside parties in. That fails here. The text only makes a clerical fix to a section heading, changing "investments" to "investment." It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a technical amendment to a statutory table of contents or section analysis, correcting a grammatical error ('investments' to 'investment'). It does not create any mechanism for outside parties to consult with, advise, or participate in federal government decisions. The reference to 'wards' estates' and 'orders of court' describes the subject matter of the referenced section, not a participation process within this section.
qwen_chat.s: The section analysis of chapter 135 of title 7, Canal Zone Code, preceding section 3081 of that title, is amended by striking out, in item numbered 8088, the word “investments”, and in lieu thereof inserting “investment”, so that the item will read: “3088. Investment awl management of wards’ estates; orders of court.”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "investment and management of wards' estates" implies some form of public participation or oversight by courts or guardians. However, this is a technical amendment to a table of contents or section analysis, merely correcting a typo ("investments" to "investment") and restating the section title. It does not establish any new process for outside parties to consult with the government, nor does it grant rights to participate in federal decision-making. The text is purely administrative and definitional.
